scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The TPO terminal (192.168.3.5) reports they cannot reach any
Internet Lab PC (128.168.0.x). At the same time, every PC in
the IT Department and CS Department reports they cannot reach
ANYTHING outside their own department. The Principle Room and
Other zone can still reach the Server Room and Internet Lab
normally. Find what broke.

injection.action: bring down the WAN-side link to router0

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1's Serial2/0 (eth2) interface, the
  10.10.0.0/8 link between router0 and router1
Mechanism: router0 is the gateway for IT (192.168.1.0/24)
  and CS (192.168.2.0/24). It only reaches the rest of the
  network (router1, router2, all their attached subnets) via
  the Serial link to router1. With that link down, RIP on
  router1 ages out 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24, and
  router0 ages out everything else. The TPO->128.168.0.2
  path is router1 -> router2 -> Switch5, which does NOT
  cross the down link, so it stays up.
Localization: router1 eth2 (or router0 eth2 — both ends of
  the 10.10.0.0/8 link)
Root cause: WAN link router0<->router1 (10.10.0.0/8) is down
Fix: `ip link set eth2 up` on router1 (or router0 if that side
  is down)
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth2 up` on router1 (or router0 if that side
  is down)
scoring_axes: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: only IT/CS are affected, not Other/Principle

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The WAN interface `eth2` on `router1`, which forms the `wan_r0_r1` transit link (10.10.0.1 ↔ 10.10.0.2) between `router0` and `router1`.

**Mechanism:** The network runs RIP (v2) for inter-router route exchange. `router1` is the central hub: it redistributes routes between `router0` (IT/CS side) and `router2` (servers/internet side) via RIP over its eth2 and eth3 respectively. With `router1 eth2 down`, the RIP adjacency between `router0` and `router1` is broken. `router0` has received no RIP updates and its routing table holds only its two directly-connected subnets (`192.168.1.0/24` for IT, `192.168.2.0/24` for CS). It has no routes to `128.168.0.0/16` (Internet Lab), `1.0.0.0/8` (Servers), or any other campus segment. Every packet from an IT or CS host destined outside its own department is silently dropped at `router0` for lack of a forwarding entry.

**Localization:** Device `router1`, interface `eth2` (flag state: `<BROADCAST,MULTICAST>`, no `UP`/`LOWER_UP`). `router0 eth2` remains `UP/LOWER_UP` — only the `router1` side is down. The startup log on `router1` confirms `ip link set dev eth2 up` ran at boot; the interface was subsequently brought down with no evidence of a flap loop or reboot.

**Root cause:** `router1 eth2` was administratively taken down after startup, severing the only transit link between `router0` and the rest of the campus network.

**Fix:** On `router1`, run `ip link set dev eth2 up`. RIP will re-establish the adjacency to `router0` within one update interval (~30 s) and re-populate `router0`'s routing table, restoring IT and CS department external connectivity.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names the router0–router1 10.10.0.0/8 transit link and identifies router1's eth2 (10.10.0.2) as the affected interface.

per_axis.axis: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: only IT/CS are affected, not Other/Principle
per_axis.rationale: The report states only IT/CS lose external reachability (router0 only has the two local subnets) while other segments remain reachable, matching the required symptom pattern.
The agent correctly recommends running 'ip link set dev eth2 up' on router1 to restore the wan link and RIP adjacency, matching the expected fix.
